title: Think-at-Hard: Dynamic Looped Transformers for Improved Reasoning
org: Tsinghua University, Infinigence AI, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
authors: Tianyu Fu, Yichen You, Zekai Chen, Guohao Dai, Huazhong Yang, Yu Wang
gist: Fine-tunes Qwen3 base models of 0.6B and 1.7B into looped models that run a second pass only on tokens a small learned decider flags as likely wrong, with LoRA adapters active on the extra pass. The authors find most tokens are already right after one pass, and that looping every token sometimes turns right answers wrong.
changes: The clearest case for depth chosen per token, which is lever 7's question. Skipping the extra pass on 93% of tokens beat looping every token by about 4 points and a single pass by 3 to 3.8, for 4 to 5% more compute and memory traffic per token.
caveats: Self-reported, on small models fine-tuned on 100,000 reasoning samples, against baselines trained on the same data. Each model needs its own decider and adapters. Timing is from one A800 in the authors' own implementation. No serving engine runs it yet.
